title: Continuous-function condensation of topological modules
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative topological ring, and work on the coherent site of profinite sets in a fixed universe large enough for the coefficients [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. A topological $R$-module here is an $R$-module $M$ with continuous addition, negation and scalar multiplication $R\times M\to M$; morphisms are continuous $R$-linear maps. Use the sheafified objectwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. There is an additive functor $\mathscr C_R$ from these topological modules to internal $\underline R$-modules with the following specified formulas.

For every $M$, its underlying abelian sheaf is $S\mapsto C(S,M)$, with restrictions by precomposition and pointwise addition. Its action $\gamma_M:\underline R\otimes\mathscr C_R(M)\to\mathscr C_R(M)$ is the unique morphism whose restriction along the canonical map from the objectwise tensor presheaf sends $a\otimes h$ to $(s\mapsto a(s)h(s))$. This action satisfies the internal unit and associativity identities, so it is defined on the sheafified tensor, without an assertion that tensor-sheaf sections equal tensor products of sections.

For every continuous $R$-linear map $f:M\to N$, the underlying map of $\mathscr C_R(f)$ on $S$ is $h\mapsto f\circ h$; this is an internal $\underline R$-linear morphism. These maps preserve identities, composition and sums.

For every finite family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ with product topology, the canonical map
$$\mathscr C_R\left(\prod_{i\in I}M_i\right)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i\in I}\mathscr C_R(M_i)$$
is an internal module isomorphism, with section map $h\mapsto(\operatorname{pr}_i\circ h)_i$ and inverse $(h_i)_i\mapsto(s\mapsto(h_i(s))_i)$. For $M=R$ with its regular action, $\mathscr C_R(R)$ is the regular internal module over $\underline R$.
